allObjections.title: Cost object underspecified
allObjections.detail: The §7 item #8 cost object defines risk_tier and blast_radius as enums but provides no canonical values or severity mapping. Without standardized enum values, different agents will interpret 'high' risk differently, leading to inconsistent recommendation filtering.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure unenforceable
allObjections.detail: The rollback.revert_procedure is a free-text string with no schema validation or step structure. CA16A-v2-CT-3 only triggers warnings for non-revertable accepted recs, but doesn't prevent operators from accepting recommendations with empty or nonsensical revert procedures.

allObjections.title: Deferred recommendations zombie problem
allObjections.detail: §7 item #8 states deferred recommendations 're-surface automatically' after defer window, but provides no mechanism to prevent infinite defer cycles. An operator could defer the same recommendation every 14 days forever, creating zombie recommendations that consume dashboard space without resolution.

allObjections.title: Multi-format confidence floor arbitrary
allObjections.detail: CA-16-C-v2-Q2's 0.85 confidence floor for target classification has no empirical basis provided. The proposal doesn't cite any testing data showing why 0.85 prevents misclassification better than 0.80 or 0.90, making this a magic number that will require constant tuning.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback mechanism in case the Redesign/Build Environment section number is deferred to engineering dispatch and later found to be incorrect. This could lead to inconsistencies in the canonical reference. (§29 numbering DEFERRED)

allObjections.title: Insufficient Validation
allObjections.detail: The minimal canonical envelope for proactive recommendations does not include sufficient validation rules, which could lead to incorrect or incomplete data being stored. (§7 Proactive Recommendations envelope)

allObjections.title: Overly Broad Classification
allObjections.detail: The 6-class Multi-Format taxonomy may be too broad, potentially leading to incorrect classification of targets. A more granular approach may be necessary to ensure accurate classification. (CA-16-C v2 Q1)

allObjections.title: Over-complication of defer-window
allObjections.detail: The introduction of a per-product defer-window for recommendations adds unnecessary complexity. Operators will struggle to manage varying defer-windows across multiple products, leading to inconsistencies. §7 item #8 + §3 admin config.

allObjections.title: Lack of rollback mechanism
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces a rollback object but does not specify a clear mechanism for rolling back accepted recommendations. This could lead to situations where accepted recommendations cause issues but cannot be easily reverted. §7 item #8.

allObjections.title: Inadequate cost estimation
allObjections.detail: The cost object includes an effort_hours_estimate, but there is no guidance on how this estimate is derived. Without a standardized method for cost estimation, the field becomes subjective and unreliable. §7 item #8.

allObjections.title: Vague operator-steerable rebuild wording
allObjections.detail: The wording for 'operator-steerable rebuild' is too vague and does not provide a concrete workflow for operators. This lack of clarity could lead to misinterpretations and inconsistent implementations. §CA-16-B v2 Q2.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide adequate details on the testing strategy for the new features, particularly for the stricter classifier and the new agent roles.

allObjections.title: Ambiguity in Rollback Mechanism
allObjections.detail: The rollback mechanism for accepted recommendations is not clearly defined, which could lead to difficulties in reverting changes if necessary.

allObjections.title: Lack of Clear Criteria for Defer-Window
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window lacks clear criteria for its application, which could lead to inconsistent use across different products.

allObjections.title: Cost object underspecified
allObjections.detail: The `cost` object in the Proactive Recommendations envelope (§7) only includes `effort_hours_estimate`, `risk_tier`, and `blast_radius`. It lacks a field for monetary cost, which is a crucial factor in evaluating recommendations.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The `rollback.revert_procedure` field in §7 is optional and human-readable. This lacks the precision needed for automated or semi-automated rollback, potentially leading to inconsistent or unreliable rollback processes.

allObjections.title: Classifier confidence floor fragility
allObjections.detail: The stricter classifier in CA-16-C-Q2, with a confidence floor of 0.85, might be too rigid. Small variations in input data could cause frequent `target_class_ambiguous` findings, overwhelming operators with dispute resolution tasks.

allObjections.title: Agent ownership rigidity
allObjections.detail: Assigning Agent #21 as the sole owner of Multi-Format target classification (CA-16-C-Q3) creates a single point of failure. If Agent #21 malfunctions or becomes outdated, the entire classification process is compromised.

allObjections.title: Crawl hard caps bypass risk
allObjections.detail: The crawl scope (§6) allows engineering to override hard caps via Doppler variables without documented approval steps. This creates an uncontrolled vector for resource exhaustion attacks if malicious actors gain access to environment configuration. The absence of runtime monitoring for crawl depth/page overrides could lead to denial-of-service on SUT infrastructure.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure gaps
allObjections.detail: The proactive recommendations rollback object (§7 item #8) permits `revertable: false` entries without mandatory justification or admin confirmation override. This violates FlowAI's reversibility principle (CA-14-B) by allowing irreversible changes via recommendations. The validation CT-3 only triggers a weak warning, insufficient for high-blast-radius changes.

allObjections.title: Cost estimation ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The new cost.effort_hours_estimate field lacks validation rules or estimation methodology requirements. Agents could emit arbitrary values (e.g., 0-hour estimates for complex features), misleading operators during disposition. This undermines the cost-benefit analysis intended by slot #14's objection resolution.

allObjections.title: Classifier severity inflation
allObjections.detail: The stricter Multi-Format classifier (§C-Q2) emits ambiguous class findings at 'high' severity unconditionally. For low-risk hybrid targets (e.g., PWAs with minor rendering quirks), this could flood operators with false-positive high-severity tickets, diluting attention from genuine critical defects.

allObjections.title: Minimal envelope lacks validation
allObjections.detail: In CA-16-A v2 §7 Proactive Recommendations, the added cost and rollback objects reference conformance tests CA16A-v2-CT-2 and CT-3 but provide no enforcement mechanism for risk_tier or revertable fields beyond a single admin warning, allowing inconsistent ProductSSOT rows across environments.

allObjections.title: Section deferral creates ambiguity
